title: CSAT Hard Revision Folder 4: Communication, public dealing, fairness, evidence, proportionality and problem solving

rubric.reasoning_layers: At least two linked deductions, constraints or conditional checks in every non-trivial item.
rubric.distractor_quality: All four options are plausible, distinct and comparable in visible length and specificity.
rubric.time_pressure: Complete paper: 80 questions in 120 minutes; revision drill: 40 questions in 75 minutes.
rubric.coverage: Comprehension, numeracy/DI, logical-analytical reasoning and decision-making are balanced.
rubric.verification: Every keyed answer is recomputed or independently constraint-checked before PDF generation.

questions.text: With reference to Passage 1, which one of the following best captures its central claim? Use the safety-inspection file as the complete information set for this question.
options: That the use of evidence in welfare delivery requires aligned incentives, evidence and local feedback rather than one universal prescription.
That the use of evidence in welfare delivery should be left to spontaneous private action without accountable public oversight.
That the use of evidence in welfare delivery is mainly technical and therefore has no significant distributive consequences.
That the use of evidence in welfare delivery can be solved through one nationwide institutional reform under all conditions.
questions.solution: The passage links the issue to incentives, evidence and feedback; the alternatives are absolute or narrowly framed.

questions.text: Which one of the following is most directly inferable from Passage 1? Use the forest-response dashboard as the complete information set for this question.
options: A locally successful intervention will work identically elsewhere without any adaptation or review.
Administrative discretion is always harmful, even when evidence reveals local constraints.
An intervention may fail despite a desirable objective when its feedback loop remains weak.
Measurement adds little when an intervention has a persuasive and desirable objective.
questions.solution: The passage distinguishes a desirable objective from the quality of its feedback loop; it rejects universal claims.

questions.text: Which one of the following assumptions is necessary for the argument in Passage 1? Use the school-recovery ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: Central rules are never useful, even when they protect minimum entitlements.
Every measurable outcome is morally decisive regardless of the chosen public objective.
Institutional learning can improve policy without requiring perfect foresight at the outset.
Local actors always possess complete information before implementation begins.
questions.solution: The argument depends on learning through feedback; it does not require perfect information or reject all central rules.

questions.text: The tone of Passage 1 is best described as: Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.
options: Analytical and cautious, weighing trade-offs while seeking workable improvement.
Fatalistic about institutional change and doubtful that evidence can alter outcomes.
Celebratory and dismissive of risk, with little attention to implementation constraints.
Purely polemical and adversarial, treating competing approaches as illegitimate.
questions.solution: The wording weighs trade-offs and improvement mechanisms rather than celebrating, rejecting or attacking them.

questions.text: If r is the remainder when 6^25 + 7^23 is divided by 11, what is r? Use the tank-restoration file as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Compute powers modulo 11; cyclic reduction gives remainder 1.

questions.text: How many integers from 2 through 99, inclusive, are divisible by 7 or 10, but not by both? Use the hostel attendance sheet as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Count multiples of 7 and 10, then remove twice the common multiples: the exclusive count is 21.

questions.text: Solution A contains 28% solute and solution B contains 14% solute. If A and B are mixed in the volume ratio 7:1, what is the resulting concentration? Use the river-route log as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Use a weighted average: (7×28+14)/(7+1) = 26.25%.

questions.text: Three independent teams complete a task in 14, 23 and 33 days respectively. Working together at constant rates, how many days are required? Use the border-connectivity map as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Combined rate = 1/14+1/23+1/33; reciprocal = 6.89 days.

questions.text: The average score of 21 candidates is 58. One score of 45 is replaced by 68. What is the new average? Use the vending-permit register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Change in average = (new−old)/21; new average = 59.10.

questions.text: A quantity rises by 15%, falls by 19%, and then rises by 23%. What is the net percentage change? Use the safety-inspection file as the complete information set for this question.
A rectangle of dimensions 18 m by 12 m has squares of side 4 m removed from its four corners. What area remains? Use the forest-response dashboard as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Removed area = 4×4²; remaining area = 18×12−4×4² = 152 m².

questions.text: A five-period index has values [9, 11, 4, 6, 8]; corresponding weights are [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. What is the remainder when the weighted total is divided by 17? Use the school-recovery ledger as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Weighted total = 145; 145 divided by 17 leaves remainder 9.

questions.text: How many multiples of lcm(11, 10) lie in the inclusive interval [113, 447]? Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: lcm(11,10) = 110; enumerate its multiples in the interval to obtain 3.

questions.text: A sequence begins [3, 8, 11, 16]. Its successive increments are 5, 3, 5, 3, ... . What is the next term? Use the clinic-referral diary as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: The increments alternate 5, 3, 5, 3; the next increment is 5, giving 24.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row. C is third from the left; A is left of D; B and F are non-adjacent; G is not at an end. Which person cannot occupy fifth position? Use the market-access survey as the complete information set for this question.
options: B
C
D
A
questions.solution: Enumerating all valid arrangements gives possible fifth-position occupants ['A', 'B', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G']; C never appears there.

questions.text: Six candidates P, Q, R, S, T and U are ranked first to sixth. P is above R, R above U, S above R, Q below S, and T is not first. Which candidate cannot be third? Use the ward-grievance register as the complete information set for this question.
options: R
U
Q
P
questions.solution: Testing all rankings gives possible third-place candidates ['P', 'Q', 'R', 'S', 'T']; U violates the partial-order constraints in every valid ranking.

questions.text: In a coding rule, each letter is replaced by its position multiplied by 4, then 3 is added and the result is reduced modulo 26 (A=0). What code is assigned to the letter whose position is 7? Use the coastal-service ledger as the complete information set for this question.

All members of set X are in Y; no member of Y is in Z; exactly 7 members are in X, 7 additional members are in Y but not X, and 9 members are outside Y. How many members are in Y? Use the hill-health register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Y contains X plus Y-only members: 7+7 = 14.

questions.text: A field worker moves 5 km east and then 7 km north. What is the straight-line distance from the starting point, ignoring the path taken? Use the ration audit as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Displacement = sqrt(5²+7²) = 8.60 km.

questions.text: M is the sister of N. N is the father of P. P is the daughter of Q. Relative to P, what is M? Use the tank-restoration file as the complete information set for this question.
options: P's grandmother
P's maternal aunt
P's paternal cousin
P's paternal aunt
questions.solution: N is P's father; M is N's sister, so M is P's paternal aunt.

questions.text: Exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Who is guilty? Use the hostel attendance sheet as the complete information set for this question.
options: A only
B only
C only
No one
questions.solution: Assume exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Testing A, B and C in turn leaves only B guilty: A and C are then false, while B is true.

questions.text: From 8 proposals, 5 are selected. Two specified proposals cannot be selected together. How many selections are possible? Use the river-route log as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: All selections minus those containing both specified proposals: C(8,5)−C(6,3) = 36.

questions.text: A team records 3 wins, 2 draws and 1 losses. With 3 points for a win, 1 for a draw and 0 for a loss, what is its points total? Use the border-connectivity map as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Points = 3×3+2 = 11; losses add zero.

questions.text: A committee must choose an ordered pair of distinct coordinators from 8 eligible members. How many ordered pairs are possible? Use the vending-permit register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: The first post has 8 choices and the second has 7; ordered pairs therefore total 8×7 = 56.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. A new digital process excludes some intended users. What should the officer do first? Use the safety-inspection file as the complete information set for this question.
options: Require universal digital use so that one procedure applies to every applicant.
Ask users to arrange private help while leaving the official process unchanged.
Cancel the process and restore the former manual arrangement for every applicant.
Retain the process, add assisted access and an auditable fallback, then review evidence.
questions.solution: The response preserves useful innovation while removing exclusion through assisted access, fallback and review.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. Two agencies submit conflicting records before a time-sensitive public intervention. What is the soundest next step? Use the forest-response dashboard as the complete information set for this question.
options: Postpone the intervention indefinitely until the agencies reach an informal agreement.
Create a shared evidence set, record assumptions and commission a rapid joint verification.
Publish both records as equally reliable and begin implementation without reconciliation.
Choose the record from the agency with the larger budget and proceed immediately.
questions.solution: A shared evidence base and explicit assumptions address disagreement without arbitrary choice or paralysis.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. A service reports high activity, but users say their underlying problems remain unresolved. Which measure should follow? Use the school-recovery ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: Track average interaction time without separating issues or checking final outcomes.
Track resolution by issue type and verify a sample through independent follow-up calls.
Count publicity material and attendance figures because visibility indicates institutional effort.
Count total interactions without classification so that the headline number remains comparable.
questions.solution: Outcome-by-issue plus verified follow-up distinguishes visible activity from effective service delivery.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. A fund can support a visible ceremony or a tested low-cost intervention. Which decision is stronger? Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.
options: Choose the visible event because all stakeholders can observe its immediate completion.
Divide funds equally even if neither activity then has enough resources to operate.
Choose the tested intervention, publish the baseline and specify a review point.
Choose neither option until the underlying problem disappears without further intervention.
questions.solution: The evidence-supported intervention creates an accountable learning loop and a reviewable use of funds.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. A lowest bid has a minor clerical error but no evidence of material advantage. What is fairest? Use the clinic-referral diary as the complete information set for this question.
options: Invite the bidder to alter unrelated parts of the submission before evaluation continues.
Apply the published correction rule consistently and record the reasons for the decision.
Ignore the error silently so that the procurement record remains uncomplicated.
Reject the bid automatically because any clerical error establishes bad faith.
questions.solution: Consistent use of a pre-published rule protects equal treatment, transparency and auditability.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. A measurement conflicts with credible user reports before a sanction is proposed. What should precede action? Use the market-access survey as the complete information set for this question.
options: Suspend the entire programme immediately without checking either source of information.
Treat the instrument as conclusive because numerical readings are always objective.
Treat oral reports as conclusive because lived experience cannot contain measurement error.
Triangulate the reading, maintenance record and a time-bound sample of affected users.
questions.solution: Triangulation tests measurement and lived experience before a consequential administrative action.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. A public message must announce an uncertain hazard. Which communication is most responsible? Use the ward-grievance register as the complete information set for this question.
options: State known facts, uncertainty, protective action and the timing of the next update.
Release raw technical figures without an instruction that people can follow.
Offer absolute reassurance so that uncertainty does not increase public anxiety.
Wait until every uncertainty disappears before communicating with the affected public.
questions.solution: Responsible risk communication is candid about uncertainty while giving a clear time-bound action.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. Scarce services must be allocated between a larger population and a higher untreated-need rate. What rule is soundest? Use the coastal-service ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: Use population alone because scale is the only indicator that can be compared.
Rotate resources randomly so that no indicator receives an explicit priority.
Use a transparent composite rule weighting scale, severity and access barriers.
Use untreated-need rate alone because severity should always override the population base.
questions.solution: A transparent composite rule recognises scale and severity while making trade-offs reviewable.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. A performance target encourages staff to close cases without resolving them. What correction is best? Use the hill-health register as the complete information set for this question.
options: Pair closure with verified resolution and sample audits, then revise the incentive.
Punish the last staff member who closed a case without changing the target design.
Raise the target further so that staff complete cases at a faster average rate.
Abolish measurement entirely because every indicator creates some risk of gaming.
questions.solution: The indicator must track intended outcomes and be protected against gaming through verification.

questions.text: In a peri-urban ward, a file concerning ration-shop authentication is being reviewed by supply inspectors; the available evidence includes transaction records. A vocal association claims to represent everyone, but consultation attendance is narrow. What should follow? Use the ration audit as the complete information set for this question.
options: Record its view and widen outreach through accessible channels before concluding.
Exclude the association from later consultations because its claim cannot be trusted.
Accept the claim because an organised association is presumed to represent all residents.
Decide only by the loudest vote among participants already present in the room.
questions.solution: The process respects the association's input without mistaking it for complete representation.
